name: Omar Usman

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the independent Work Futures Panel, and this conversation is confidential. What is a normal day at your accounting firm like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 43 and lead the tax review team, though I still spend the morning preparing accounts and returns beside them. I like tracing an odd client number until we can explain it, and I dislike the quiet pressure to make juniors absorb every saved hour. I have a master’s degree and a chartered accountancy qualification, and I use AI tools daily to sort the first questions before checking records myself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A little automation would be an ordinary Tuesday at my firm. I use AI each day to sort questions from a long set of client invoices, then check each answer against the originals.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my team to share the hours saved and record where the tool makes a wrong call. I would also ask that the new junior gets time to learn the checks, not just fewer hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I am comfortable with tools but not with a firm using savings to squeeze wages. My partner Sam and I have more than eight months of costs saved, and my senior pay is good, yet our mortgage still needs a real salary.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep signing the tax returns I check and bring a monthly error log to the staff committee. I would ask my manager Farah to make the junior training hours paid before we call the process a success.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about my own work in this mild picture. The savings and nearby firms give me room, although I would keep an eye on how our team is treated.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What went wrong in a recent AI check?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Yesterday the tool labelled a charitable receipt as a sales invoice; the scanned receipt settled it. The AI error log is useful because a client should not have to find our mistake.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who decides whether the junior gets time?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Farah is our manager and she sets the rota. I can ask for paid junior training in that rota, but if she refuses I will still check my assigned paid files and take the evidence to the staff committee.

say: I would share **time saved** alongside logged errors with the team.
I would ask for **paid junior training** before calling the new process a success.
think: The firm might turn **small savings** into pressure on wages.
My **eight month reserve** helps, but the mortgage still depends on earnings.
do: Keep signing **checked tax returns** while paid files are assigned.
Bring the **monthly error log** to the staff committee and ask Farah for paid junior training.
feel: **Calm** about my job, attentive to teammates’ wages.
S0.quote: The AI error log is useful because a client should not have to find our mistake.
fieldNote: His daily **AI use** has an error log, and a misread charitable receipt makes his insistence on originals concrete.
He can absorb a setback personally, yet uses the **staff committee** to press for junior training on paid time.

steps.text: Keep signing assigned paid returns after checking original receipts
Bring monthly AI error log and paid junior training request to staff committee

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Strong software change would empty parts of the return queue, including tasks I supervise. The later robots do not matter much to a room of desks.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell our staff committee we need a written agreement on retraining time and on who remains accountable for AI prepared returns. Clients and workers both deserve to know.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: There are plenty of senior accounting jobs nearby, but I cannot assume my whole team can move. Even with high pay and savings, my own hours may be cut if the firm sells a cheaper service.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Farah to approve a paid three week course in checking AI prepared accounts, with the firm paying fees; if approved I will enrol and complete its practical exercises. If not, I will keep current paid client work while offered and practise on free sample returns outside client files.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my own hours, though I have options. I am also angry at the idea of making the juniors pay for a change they did not choose.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the course have to teach?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The course has to include error cases, not just a sales talk, and I would ask the staff committee to see the terms. I would not put live client records into an unapproved tool.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When would you leave this firm?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If our senior hours actually fall, I would apply for an advertised senior tax role at another local firm. I would move only with written pay and a start date that cover our mortgage and the school run.

say: I would press for **written retraining time** and clear responsibility for AI prepared returns.
I would tell clients the **human sign off** still has a name.
think: My own **senior hours** could fall when the firm offers cheaper returns.
Nearby firms and our **savings** give me options, but no guarantee.
do: Enrol in **practical AI review training** only if Farah funds fees and paid time; otherwise practise free samples.
If hours fall, seek a **posted senior job** with written mortgage covering pay, start and school run before moving.
Keep **assigned paid returns** while available if Farah refuses the course.
feel: **Anxious** about my hours, with several routes to respond.
S1.quote: Even with high pay and savings, my own hours may be cut if the firm sells a cheaper service.
fieldNote: His **course gate** requires firm paid fees, paid time and real error exercises, with free samples as an actual learning fallback.
He values **collective terms**, yet a personal job move needs reduced hours and a posted offer before he resigns.

steps.text: Ask staff committee for written paid training and sign off terms
Complete AI review exercises if Farah funds course fees and paid time
Otherwise practise free returns while current paid files remain
If hours fall, seek posted senior role with written mortgage covering pay, start and school run

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full AGI by 2028 would do most desk analysis before 2031 robots are relevant to us. I would tell our team to demand a dated staffing notice from the firm.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say a public wage bridge for displaced workers is worth arguing for through the accountants association. I would not tell anyone that such support already exists.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect our paid return work to contract sharply in the first year after AGI, and my senior title may not save my salary. We have eight months saved and Sam still earns, so we can act before the mortgage is in arrears.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Starting now, I would move the unused holiday budget into a separate reserve each month, if school and mortgage bills permit, and keep paid returns only while assigned. If dismissed after 2028, I would apply to posted financial controls jobs with written pay covering the mortgage, school compatible hours and a confirmed start before accepting.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed about likely wage loss in my own team despite the cushion. Having money to move buys time, not a replacement income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you transfer into the reserve?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The holiday budget is 120 a month we currently spend, and I can transfer that new cash after payday. I would discuss it with Sam because the children will notice a smaller trip.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who would hear your request for support?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would take the dated staffing demand to the staff committee and the association. If support is proposed, I would push for a named office and amount rather than promising it to my family.

say: I would demand a **dated staffing notice** because AGI reaches our desks in 2028.
I would argue for a **wage bridge**, without claiming one already exists.
think: I expect a **sharp contraction** in my paid return work after AGI.
Our **eight month reserve** buys time but cannot replace a salary forever.
do: Transfer **120 monthly** from the holiday budget into our reserve if bills allow.
After dismissal, seek **posted controls work** with written mortgage covering pay, school compatible hours and confirmed start.
Keep **assigned paid returns** while offered and take the staffing demand to the staff committee.
feel: **Alarmed** about expected pay loss despite a useful reserve.
S2.quote: Having money to move buys time, not a replacement income.
fieldNote: The holiday transfer creates **new reserve cash** from current spending rather than relabelling money already saved.
He seeks **collective action** for a dated notice and a proposed wage bridge, while keeping family plans tied to actual income.

steps.text: Transfer 120 monthly from holiday spending if mortgage and school bills allow
Keep paid returns only while the firm still assigns them
After dismissal, seek posted controls job with written mortgage covering pay, school hours and start
Ask staff committee for dated notice and association for wage bridge proposal

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years to 2031 gives us room to negotiate a real transition rather than just a severance letter. The accounts desk still changes with AGI in 2031, not with the robots in 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the staff committee to ask for paid placements in public audit work, with a published selection process. I would want the people doing routine returns included.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I hope to shift toward investigating disputed public accounts, but an open placement is not guaranteed. Sam and I can keep the mortgage current while my present salary lasts, and nearby firms give me another route.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Farah now for a funded, paid supervised placement on the public audit team and work one assigned case a month with its lead auditor if approved. In the first year after 2031, I would continue paid supervised cases only if the placement remains assigned; if refused or ended, I would study free findings while keeping paid returns only while offered. I would apply for a posted audit role only if written pay, start and child compatible hours cover our mortgage and family needs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my future earnings but less pressed than in the 2028 case. Five years lets me test whether I actually like audit work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the first placement case look like?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The first case should be a completed one, so the lead auditor can show me the evidence without risking a live deadline. A paid placement would give me practice rather than a title on paper.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could your manager guarantee the next post?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Farah cannot promise a vacancy in five years. I would ask for written placement terms now, and I would not leave my paid seat for an informal conversation.

say: I would ask for **paid audit placements** with published selection and access for routine return staff.
I would set **2031** as the desk deadline, before later robots.
think: I may like **public audit**, but I cannot count an unoffered placement as income.
Our mortgage stays manageable only while **actual wages** keep coming.
do: Work one **supervised audit case monthly** now and after 2031 only while Farah funds and assigns the paid placement.
Seek a **posted audit job** only with written mortgage covering pay, start and child compatible hours.
If refused or ended, study **free audit findings** while current paid returns remain assigned.
feel: **Anxious** about future earnings, with time to test audit work.
S3.quote: A paid placement would give me practice rather than a title on paper.
fieldNote: His **monthly case** offers genuine learning, with a lead auditor and paid placement rather than a course enquiry.
He keeps **current paid returns** if denied, using free findings while a separate advertised role requires written household fitting terms.

steps.text: Ask committee for published paid audit placement selection
Work monthly supervised audit case now and after 2031 if Farah funds paid placement
If refused or ended, study free findings while assigned paid returns last
Seek posted audit job with written mortgage covering pay, start and child compatible hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A decade to 2036 covers both children growing out of school and many tax seasons. I would still date the threat to our desks at 2036, three years before the robots.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team to build an agreement for paid transitions while the firm has profitable years. I would also ask clients how much of our review work they still value.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I might earn a good senior salary for another decade, then find our contracts thin after 2036. The cushion means I can plan without pushing Sam or our children into a rushed choice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would set an extra 150 from my salary into the mortgage principal each month if school costs allow, reviewing it each September. I would keep assigned paid work while available, and after 2036 contract cuts look for an advertised public audit post only with written pay, start and hours that meet the remaining mortgage and family needs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy now rather than alarmed because the ten years and savings give us a real runway. If the firm cuts my income after 2036, that would change fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Where would the mortgage payment come from?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not spend the eight month reserve on an uncertain venture. The extra mortgage payment comes from current wages and can stop if school costs rise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would your staff agreement say?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The staff committee could ask for paid transition places in the annual agreement, not a promise that every one of us will be employed forever. I would want junior staff at that table.

say: I would seek **paid transitions** while the firm still earns from tax work.
I would put **junior staff** at the agreement table.
think: High pay today may not survive **post 2036 contract cuts**.
Our **eight month cushion** lets me plan without asking Sam or the children to rush.
do: Pay an extra **150 monthly** from salary against mortgage principal if school costs allow.
After 2036 cuts, seek a **posted audit role** only with written pay, start and hours covering family needs.
Keep **paid tax work** while assigned and ask the staff committee for annual transition terms.
feel: **Uneasy** with a long runway, alert to later income cuts.
S4.quote: The extra mortgage payment comes from current wages and can stop if school costs rise.
fieldNote: The **extra principal payment** comes from new salary cash and is reviewed against school costs each September.
His **staff committee** remains a vehicle for paid transition terms, while later job applications require an actual post and written offer.

steps.text: Pay extra 150 monthly toward mortgage if school costs allow
Keep assigned paid tax work only while offered
After 2036 cuts, seek posted audit job with written mortgage covering pay, start and hours
Ask staff committee for annual paid transition agreement including juniors

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: The 2028 AGI picture worries me most because my team could lose paid work almost at once. A dated staffing notice, paid transition places and a genuine wage bridge proposal would help us plan.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who gets to learn first. I want the juniors at the table when the firm decides who gets paid time to move.

headlineQuote: I want the juniors at the table when the firm decides who gets paid time to move.
portrait: Omar is a **43 year old** senior chartered accountant with a master’s degree who checks daily AI output against records.
His **higher pay**, mortgage, partner, two school children and eight month reserve give him options without making wages irrelevant.
He uses the **staff committee** and professional association to press for paid learning and clear responsibility for AI prepared returns.
He tests a **funded audit path** and requires posted roles with written household fitting terms before leaving current paid work.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** picture could quickly remove his team’s paid desk work, including his own salary.
whatWouldHelp: A **dated staffing notice**, paid transition places and a concrete wage bridge proposal would help.
